title: QUANTITY OF ART POTTERY PLATES...
reason: Large lot of handmade studio pottery with two named potters in the title; attribution unverified (no marks visible) but the quality is good and it could be worth more than a general lot price if the names are collectable.
findings: About 20 pieces of handmade glazed studio-style pottery. Photo 1 overview: a large dark charger with blue, brown and gold streaky glaze at the back; about 9 to 10 black plates and saucers with red and blue splash glaze in two sizes; at least 2 (possibly 4) cream plates with painted pink flowers and a black half glaze; 2 matching mugs in the same floral and navy glaze; a small grey cup with a gold rim that looks like a different, commercial piece; 2 stacked bowls (blue and cream floral interior with a purple-brown rim, lower bowl with a green and cream swirl exterior); and a large yellow-rimmed pierced footed bowl or colander with a blue interior and two applied rolled handles. Photo 6 shows the underside of the pierced bowl: glazed, hollow foot with pierced holes, no signature, stamp or incised mark seen. No signatures, impressed or painted marks or labels are visible on any piece in the six photos (plate undersides are not shown). The catalogue names Jill Spencer and Catherine Batten, but the photos do not show which pieces are theirs, so the attributions are unverified, and I could not research the potters (web search budget was used up). Glazing quality is good and the black splash-glaze plates look like one potter's set.
condition: No chips or cracks visible on the faces shown. Glaze pitting and bubbles on the black plates (look like part of the glaze effect). Handle ends on the pierced bowl show raw clay (looks like the design but worth checking for breaks). Undersides and rims not fully checked.
rescore_note: About 20 pieces of competent handmade studio pottery (large streaky charger, about 10 black red and blue splash plates, floral plates and mugs, pierced footed bowl) with no signature, mark or label visible in any of the six photos, so the Jill Spencer and Catherine Batten attributions are unverified and could not be researched (web search budget was used up); valued as decorative pottery at my estimate of about $50 to $100.
